title: Joint window tests retain four late OI v2 correction signs across three dependence choices
abstract: We tested feedback correction signs in 21 overlapping 21-year SST windows from 1982-2002 through 2002-2022. We used signed aggregate SST and five-model radiation series. We held correction paths fixed and tested a linear contrast whose sign equals the feedback difference when both warming trends are positive. Shared Gaussian time weights preserve overlap. A maximum-statistic band covers all contrast and warming statistics within each product family under a fitted covariance model. With three-year dependence, 20 of 42 DOISST comparisons have marginal signs and 11 have joint signs. No window retains a sign for both DOISST correction fits with all two-, three- and five-year dependence choices. For OI v2, all three choices retain a negative raw-minus-corrected sign in four windows, from 1999-2019 through 2002-2022. These results limit broad window claims but support the late OI correction sign under the tested assumptions. Joint coverage is approximate for climate data. Corrections, model responses and the mask are fixed, and no new SST observations are used.

display.caption: Signed contrast statistics across overlapping windows. Joint thresholds include numerator and warming uncertainty. Dependence length is three years.
